title: fix(plugin-email, service-sms): Send test goes to the signed-in admin when the request names no recipient
body:
Part of #24767

Clause-②: no

This lands half A of the card, the two Send test actions. Half B, the Mail save that succeeds with its required fields empty, is left open: it is the settings save gate working as designed, and changing it is a decision about `settings-service.ts`, which this claim does not hold. The section below has the measurement.

## Half A: Send test had no recipient

The Mail and SMS settings pages offer **Send test** and no recipient input. The served console posts its unsaved edits as the action body (`runSettingsAction(namespace, actionId, draft)`, objectui `apps/console/src/pages/settings/SettingsView.tsx` at the pinned `.objectui-sha` `12dc7b47c3`), so the request carries no `to`:

- `mail/test` (`plugin-email`) read `ctx.body.to ?? payload.to ?? from_email`. It mailed the test to the From address (the sender, often a no-reply mailbox), or refused with `Provide a "to" address (or set from_email).` when From was empty.
- `sms/test` (`service-sms`) read `ctx.body.to ?? payload.to` and refused every press from the served form.

**Now:** when the request names no `to`, the test goes to the person who pressed the button. `mail/test` sends to the caller's own `sys_user.email`, and `sms/test` sends to the caller's own `sys_user.phone_number`, the column the messaging `sms` channel delivers to. A `to` in the body still wins.

- The read is `findOne('sys_user', { where: { id: ctx.userId }, fields: [ONE_COLUMN] })` under the system opt-in. `where.id` is the caller's own id from the settings context, never a value the body names. So the one value it returns is the caller's own address or number, and the SMS answer masks the number.
- Every refusal that remains says that nothing was sent and what to supply. A failed account read is reported as a failed read, never as "no address".
- A number is on an account only where phone sign-in (the opt-in `phoneNumber` auth plugin) is enabled. On other deployments "Send test SMS" still refuses from the served form. The refusal now says why, where before it asked for a field the page does not have.

**Two riders on the same handler.** The recipient default makes both reachable from the served form:

- With the log-only transport (the namespace's default `None (log only)` provider), `sms/test` answered `ok: true`, "Sent test SMS … via log", and delivered nothing. It now answers `ok: false` with severity `warning` and sends nothing. `mail/test` already follows this rule for its `LogTransport`.
- When the form names no delivering provider, the transport the deployment configured at boot carries the test. The success message still said "via log" in that case. It now names the deployment's configured transport.

**Also removed: `ctx.body.to`.** `SettingsService.runAction` hands a handler a `SettingsContext`, which has no `body`, so no route ever reached that read. `MailSettingsSurface` now types the handler context as `{ userId?: string }`. Two queue-delivery tests passed `to` that way, and now pass it as `payload.to`, the channel the route uses.

**Unchanged:**

- No setting, route, spec key or manifest key is added.
- None of the claim's hard stops was edited: `settings-service.ts`, `settings-service-plugin.ts`, `packages/spec/**`, objectui.

## Half B: why it is left open

The measurement used a real `SettingsService` with the real `mail` manifest and a fresh in-memory store, on objectstack `87c09ebb7a` (`packages/services/service-settings/dist` built from that commit). Each console save was replayed as `setMany('mail', DIRTY_KEYS)`:

| Console save (its dirty keys only) | Answer | `smtp_host` / `from_email` afterwards |
|---|---|---|
| `from_name`, `smtp_port`, `smtp_secure`, `smtp_user` or `queue_delivery` alone | saved | both still empty |
| `provider: 'smtp'` | `SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, `smtp_host` `required` | unchanged |
| `provider: 'resend'` | `SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, `api_key` `required` | unchanged |
| `from_email: ''` | `SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, `from_email` `required` | unchanged |
| `smtp_host: ''` | `SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, `smtp_host` `required` | unchanged |
| `smtp_host: 'smtp.example.com'` | saved | `from_email` still empty |

- **It is not a manifest defect.** `smtp_host` and `from_email` both declare `required: true` in `mail.manifest.ts`.
- **It is the documented TOUCH gate** in `SettingsService.validatePatch`: "A specifier is checked only when the patch TOUCHES it — its own key is in the patch, or a key its `visible` expression references is". The console posts only its dirty keys. So a save that edits From name, Port, TLS, Username or the queue toggle never touches the empty required fields, and Branding's refusal is the same gate on a key the save does write.
- **The choice goes to the decision frame.** Every route that changes this lands in `validatePatch` (`settings-service.ts`) or in the console. Neither is this claim's, so this PR does not close the card. The choice, with its four axes, is in the dev report on the card.

## Pins, on the real service and the real routes

Each suite builds a real `SettingsService` with the real manifest and mounts its real routes through `registerSettingsRoutes`. The real plugin then registers its action at `kernel:ready`. Each case presses `POST /api/settings/NS/test` with the body the console sends.

- `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/mail-test-recipient.pin.test.ts`:
  - With body `{}`, the answer is 200, `ok: true`, and nodemailer is handed the admin's own address, never From. The `sys_user` read is pinned to the caller's id and the `email` column.
  - Control: `{ to }` wins, and no account is read.
  - The refusal cases each answer 400 with the ADR-0112 envelope (`success: false`, `error.code: SETTINGS_ACTION_FAILED`, `error.details` carrying `ok: false`), and nothing is sent: no address, no account row, a failed account read. An in-process call with no user also refuses.
- `packages/services/service-sms/src/sms-test-recipient.pin.test.ts`:
  - The same shape over a Twilio draft: the `To` Twilio receives is the admin's own number, and it is masked in the answer.
  - Control: `{ to }` wins.
  - The refusal cases answer 400 `SETTINGS_ACTION_FAILED` and send nothing: no number, no account row, a failed read. The log-only provider answers severity `warning`.
- `packages/services/service-sms/src/sms-plugin.test.ts`:
  - The log-only test no longer pins `ok: true`. It now pins `ok: false`, `warning`, and that the transport was never called.
  - A new case pins that a boot-configured Twilio transport is not reported "via log".
- The new mail double routes `update` and `findOne` through `assertEngineUpdateDispatch` and `assertEngineFindOnePredicate`. `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` records the two rows (`check-engine-double-contract --write`: 2 added, 0 lost).

## Ablation: one leg per behaviour changed

Each leg was a committed tree, mutated by `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the anchor hit 1 → 0 and the blob changed. Each was restored with `git checkout HEAD -- PATH`, and the restore was proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. The subject is imported by relative path, so no build sits between mutation and measurement.

| Leg | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| mail default recipient | the `from_email` fallback put back | 5 of 6 mail pins red, control green |
| SMS default recipient | caller id withheld from the resolver | the default-recipient pin red (and the log case, which then refuses on the recipient first) |
| SMS log rule | the `LogSmsTransport` check disabled | both log pins red |
| SMS transport label | `via` put back to the form's provider | the label pin red |

## Verification at `f0128702e5`

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-email exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 35 files, 577 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-sms exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 7 files, 103 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-email run typecheck` and the same for `@objectstack/service-sms`: exit 0, both test layers OK. The new pin files are in each `tsconfig.test.json` program, counted with `--listFiles`.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 76 commands. All 76 ran with their exit captured before any pipe, and every one exited 0. `--ran` answered "76 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero …)".
- The closure was built first with `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/plugin-email^...' --filter '@objectstack/service-sms^...' --filter '@objectstack/service-settings^...' build`, after merging `origin/main` at `08d201a80e`.
- Gate families CI runs are left to the PR's check-runs.

## Acceptance notes

- **The console does not honour an `action_button` handler's declared shape.** The console ignores `SpecifierHandlerSchema`'s `http` `body`, `url`, `method` and `confirmText`. It posts `draft` to `/api/settings/NS/ACTION` whatever the handler declares. Every in-repo manifest's handler URL is that path, and none declares `body` or `confirmText`, so nothing visible diverges today. That is zero pull, so it is not filed. It is also why "a recipient carried by the existing payload contract" is not a route here: `body` interpolates against stored namespace values and request context, and no renderer reads it.
- **The SMS fallback stub still reports a success it did not have.** `smsTestActionHandler` (the service-settings fallback) still answers `ok: true`, "Configuration looks valid … Wire @objectstack/service-sms for actual delivery". It runs only where `SmsServicePlugin` registers no action: no SMS plugin, or a host-injected transport. `sms` is always-on, so a served boot mounts the plugin, and no public door into the injected-transport composition was measured. This is a read-only inference. Carrier: none.
- **The suggested "verified address" is not applied.** The address read is the caller's own. The action is gated by the namespace's write permission, whose holder can already name any `to`. The messaging email channel delivers to `sys_user.email` with no verification check either. So a verification requirement would add no protection the gate does not already give, and it would refuse the test for an admin whose own address is unverified.
- **Related card:** objectstack-ai/objectui#13145 remains open. It is the opposite edge of the half B rule: clearing a saved value is refused.
